MODULE 4: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-2 SHOOTING

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

#### EQUIPMENT

2 balls per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will space in the left corner, left wing and left slot. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from side-line to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. Two defenders will begin with the ball and position themselves close to the offensive players. The defense will pass the ball to any offensive player. The offense has a maximum of four dribbles to find a ROB shot. Stay for three repetitions in a row before changing roles. Players may step into range to shoot the ball if they cannot shoot the 3PT but they must re-space beyond the 3PT line after passing the ball.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Every offensive player has two dribbles per catch, and can either catch-and-shoot or drive for a lay-up.
- Offensive players are allowed to cut.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players space in the correct starting location.
- Ensure players do not travel.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where was the open pass?"
- "Defensively, can you find a way to trick the offense when closing out?"

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating spacing and advantage
- Disruptive defense
- Attacking closeouts

MODULE 4: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

4-ON-4 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS WITH A RANDOM START

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four players, based on the number of courts available. Four offensive players will space in varied locations outside the 3PT line, with four defenders guarding them and another team of four waiting along the baseline. The offense has a 14 second shot clock to score. If the defense gains possession (defensive rebound or forced turnover), they must clear the ball before the shot clock starts again. On a score, the team that gets scored on rotates off, while the new team sprints onto defense.

EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- After each score, the activity begins with a dynamic start (e.g. sideline inbounds, baseline inbounds or shooting a free-throw).
- When playing off a free-throw, there is no out of bounds or requirement to inbound the ball).
- Teams can be given actions to run and to emphasize as they play (on-ball screen, off-ball screen, blitz the ball-handler, etc.)

SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

STAFF ROLE

- Count down from 14 seconds.
- Help players utilize and incorporate dynamic starts.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

KEY CONCEPTS

- Players standing in space to prevent one defender guarding two offensive players at the same time
- Creating advantages through 1-on-1 or post-ups

GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you create an advantage faster within the 14 second clock?"
- "What ways can we disrupt the offense within their 1-on-1 drives from the perimeter or post-ups?"

MODULE 4: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get a point. The losing team rotates off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining excellent spacing
- Containing defensive match-ups 1-on-1

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add a +1 offensive player to provide an advantage to both teams.
- Scores off post-ups are worth double.
- Scores in transition are worth double.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you get the most efficient shot?"
- "How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?"
- "What can you do to space the floor effectively?"

MODULE 4: FULL OUTLINE

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!

## TIP-OFF

is our opening huddle where coaches welcome the players as a group and set the expectations for the day. The Tip-Off should take no longer than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are 5 parts that should be covered in every Tip-Off:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!
